tool_args.old_string: Paired improvements ($\tau$-gated vs.\ VLA-only) reach statistical significance on Spatial ($p{=}0.017$, Appendix~\ref{sec:8seed}) but not on other suites at $n{=}3$. The finding applies to the tested MLP-based CRM; larger architectures may differ. The method requires stochastic VLAs (Appendix~\ref{sec:applicability}), $\tau$ is suite-dependent (Appendix~\ref{sec:tau_sweep}), and recovery on $\pi_{0.5}$ is partial (Table~\ref{tab:tau_sweep_pi05}). All experiments use LIBERO simulation; real-robot transfer and adaptive $\tau$ selection remain future work.
tool_args.new_string:
\looseness=-1 \textbf{Statistical power.} Paired improvements ($\tau$-gated vs.\ VLA-only) reach statistical significance on Spatial ($p{=}0.017$, Appendix~\ref{sec:8seed}) but not on other suites at $n{=}3$ seeds. Increasing the seed count would sharpen confidence intervals but is computationally expensive given LIBERO's per-seed evaluation cost.

\looseness=-1 \textbf{Architecture scope.} The finding applies to the tested MLP-based CRM (${\sim}$327K parameters); larger or more expressive correction architectures (e.g., transformer-based residual modules) may exhibit different failure modes. Similarly, the CRM is trained with $L_2$ loss on demonstration actions; alternative training objectives could shift the correction quality distribution.

\looseness=-1 \textbf{Stochastic VLA requirement.} The $K{=}2$ pairwise distance probe requires diverse stochastic samples; deterministic VLAs such as OpenVLA-OFT produce near-identical outputs across draws, yielding no usable uncertainty signal (Appendix~\ref{sec:applicability}). Extending calibrated gating to deterministic VLAs would require alternative uncertainty sources.

\looseness=-1 \textbf{Threshold and generalization.} The threshold $\tau$ is suite-dependent (Appendix~\ref{sec:tau_sweep}), and recovery on $\pi_{0.5}$ is partial (Table~\ref{tab:tau_sweep_pi05}). All experiments use LIBERO simulation with scripted demonstrations; real-robot transfer, adaptive $\tau$ selection, and evaluation on human-collected data remain future work.

85	Figure~\ref{fig:trigger_scatter} visualizes the mechanism: trigger rate correlates monotonically with effect size. Suites with high uncertainty (trigger ${>}$7\%: Spatial, Goal) see positive corrections; confident suites (trigger ${<}$5\%: Object, Long) preserve baseline, avoiding the catastrophic $-$14.8\,pp and $-$4.7\,pp degradation of unconditional correction. SR is robust to $\tau$ choice, varying by ${\leq}$2\,pp on Spatial as trigger rate changes $5.5{\times}$ (Appendix~\ref{sec:tau_sweep}).
86	
87	The suite-level pattern reflects task-specific uncertainty structure. Spatial tasks require precise placement relative to landmarks, producing genuinely diverse candidates when the VLA hesitates; the CRM resolves this ambiguity productively. Object tasks involve novel instances where pretrained representations generalize well, yielding confident predictions that correction can only perturb. Long---where the CRM is out-of-distribution---confirms that gating effectiveness depends jointly on VLA uncertainty quality and CRM coverage.
88	
89	\paragraph{Efficiency.}
90	\label{sec:magnitude_results}
